claim.pdf_says: Page 1018 (printed 988) ends with "Psalter_Pahlavi:\n10B80-10B91" and nothing further. "Rejang:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1019 (printed 989), directly above "A930-A946".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1018 block: "Psalter_Pahlavi:\n10B80-10B91 Rejang:" - with "Rejang:" glued to the end of Psalter_Pahlavi's range line. The page-1019 block then opens with a headless "A930-A946".
claim.why_it_matters: Same normative-annex structural corruption as the Old_Italic case: the script name Rejang is detached from its code-point range A930-A946 and appended to a different script's entry on the previous page. A reader or extractor working page by page sees Psalter_Pahlavi's line polluted and Rejang's range unattributed.

verdict.reasoning: Independently verified on both sides at 300 dpi; I set out to refute this and could not. PDF EVIDENCE. Page 1018 (printed folio 988), rendered via scripts/spec/page_workunit.py: the last two printed body lines are 'Psalter_Pahlavi:' and, beneath it, '10B80-10B91'. I read the printed glyphs directly - that line terminates at the final 'F'... 'exactly at 10B80-10B91' with nothing following it; below is blank space to the bottom margin, then the footer '988  (C)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license watermark. No 'Rejang' token is printed anywhere on page 1018. Page 1019 (printed folio 989): the first body line under the right-aligned running head is 'Rejang:', and the line directly beneath it is 'A930-A946' - an intact two-line entry wholly on page 1019, laid out exactly like every other entry in the list. MARKDOWN EVIDENCE. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40609 'Psalter_Pahlavi:', line 40610 '10B80-10B91 Rejang:', line 40611 blank, lines 40612-40614 the page-1019 furniture, line 40615 blank, line 40616 a bare 'A930-A946'. Both halves of the claim are quoted exactly; neither source is misquoted. WHY THE STANDARD REJECTION GROUNDS DO NOT APPLY. (a) Not reflow or line wrapping: '10B80-10B91' is a complete line terminated by a page end and 'Rejang:' is a complete line opening the next page, so the merged line '10B80-10B91 Rejang:' exists nowhere in the PDF and no wrapping convention produces it. (b) Not curable by stripping page furniture: delete the anchor, '## Page 1019' and the running head and you are still left with '10B80-10B91 Rejang:' followed by a blank line and an orphan 'A930-A946' - the blank-line entry separator, which is the only structure this table has, sits in the wrong place. Correct recovery needs a special-case rule ('a trailing Name: token on a range line owns the next block's first range') that parses nothing else in the document. (c) It does change meaning, and the loss is NOT recoverable by cross-reference. This is one of three related script tables in the file, and they carry DIFFERENT values for Rejang: this table (line 40610 region) binds Rejang to A930-A946; a second table binds Rejang to A947-A953 (lines 40974-40975); a third binds it to A930-A953 (lines 49409-49410). An extractor that loses the binding here cannot reconstruct A930-A946 from the siblings - it would recover a wrong range. (d) Page attribution is load-bearing in this file: the document's own index cites page anchors (e.g. '[1019](#page-1019)'), so content filed under the wrong anchor is a citation-integrity defect, not formatting. MECHANISM, PRECISELY CHARACTERIZED. A uniform extractor off-by-one emits the first printed line of page N+1 at the tail of page N's block and joins it to the preceding line. Confirmed instances: line 40481-ish 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:' (1014/1015), 'x10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:' (1015/1016), '10980-1099F Miao:' (1016/1017), line 40558 '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:' (1017/1018), line 40610 '10B80-10B91 Rejang:' (1018/1019), line 40981 'A880-A881, A8B4-A8C5, A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:', and line 49374 '10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:' (1219/1220). Crucially it correctly does NOT fire at 1019/1020 or 1020/1021: the PDF itself ends those pages with an orphaned label ('Tai_Le:', 'Yezidi:') so page N+1 opens with a range, and the markdown reproduces that faithfully. Only a LABEL line migrates. That the artifact tracks the PDF layout this exactly proves it is a transcription defect with a known trigger, not noise - and makes it mechanically sweepable.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED as described. Three refinements for the ledger. (1) Calibrate the impact: no characters are lost. This is a misplacement plus a line merge, not a deletion - the token sequence '...10B80-10B91 Rejang: ... A930-A946' is all present in file order, and a human reading linearly still recovers both bindings. What is corrupted is line structure, blank-line entry grouping, and page attribution, and therefore the machine-readable name-to-range association. 'Structural' is the right severity; it must not be read as 'text missing'. (2) The defect is systematic at page boundaries throughout this annex, not specific to Rejang, and it has an exactly identifiable trigger: whenever a page ends with a complete entry and the next page opens with a script-name line, that name line is pulled back and joined to the previous page's last range line, leaving the next page's block opening with an unattributed range. Confirmed sites: 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:' (1014/1015), '...10760-10767 Linear_B:' (1015/1016), '10980-1099F Miao:' (1016/1017), line 40558 '...10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:' (1017/1018), line 40610 '10B80-10B91 Rejang:' (1018/1019), line 40981 '...A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:', and line 49374 '10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:' (1219/1220). It correctly does not fire at 1019/1020 or 1020/1021, where the PDF itself orphans the label at the page foot ('Tai_Le:', 'Yezidi:') and the markdown matches. Fix by sweeping the pattern /^[0-9A-Fa-f][0-9A-Fa-f,\- ]*\s+[A-Za-z][A-Za-z_]*:\s*$/ on the last content line before a page anchor - split the trailing label onto its own line and move it into the FOLLOWING page block - rather than patching the two or three known sites. (3) Cross-check warning: the file contains three distinct script tables with DIFFERENT ranges for the same script names - Rejang is A930-A946 here (the affected site), A947-A953 at lines 40974-40975, and A930-A953 at lines 49409-49410, with Psalter_Pahlavi and Old_Italic likewise repeated. The later, correctly-transcribed occurrences are NOT evidence that this site is fine, and the orphaned 'A930-A946' must not be reconciled against the A930-A953 entry when repairing.
